question: Does the cluster-selected, Solar-screened isothermal law predict untouched outer rotation-curve points across distinct SPARC galaxy morphologies without retuning its gravity constants?

law.lambda_source: results/solar_screened_isothermal/report.json; selected on MACS0329 and MACS0429 before this SPARC morphology score
law.source_mass_definition: 1.33*MHI + Upsilon_disk*L_disk + Upsilon_bulge*L_bulge, with only standard inner-fit baryonic nuisances and distance scaling
law.geometry: SPARC tabulated gas, disk, and bulge radial force components set gbar; the added tail is source-centered and spherical

claim_boundary: This is an inner-calibrated radial prediction test, not a new-galaxy prediction test.
The morphology bins were fixed before the screened-law SPARC scores were computed.
The outer-rotation-shape bin is descriptive because it is defined using observed velocities.
SPARC supplies in-plane axisymmetric disk and bulge force templates; this test does not predict vertical dynamics or non-axisymmetric bars and spirals.
The spherical added tail does not independently respond to disk thickness or bulge shape.
The NFW control fits two halo parameters per galaxy on inner points and is not a general test of dark matter.
The Solar result remains a first-order Mercury and force-fraction diagnostic, not a raw multi-planet ephemeris fit.
